name: Perturbed Friedmann Universe in Bardeen's Potentials
description: A Friedmann universe with two small gravitational potentials laid over it, kept to first order in them. It is the spacetime in which the fluctuations of the microwave background and the growth of structure are calculated, and in the longitudinal gauge its two potentials are Bardeen's gauge invariants.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit and every quantity to first order in the potentials. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history:
A Friedmann universe with a small gravitational potential laid over it is the geometry in which the fluctuations of the microwave background and the growth of structure are calculated [ma1995, mukhanov1992]. In the longitudinal gauge its line element is $ds^2 = a^2(\eta)\left[-(1 + 2\Phi)\,d\eta^2 + (1 - 2\Psi)\,\delta_{ij}\,dx^idx^jight]$, with $\eta$ the conformal time, $a\,d\eta = c\,dt$, and $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ small functions of all four coordinates [mukhanov1992, ma1995]. In the Newtonian limit $\Phi$ is the Newtonian potential over $c^2$, which is where the gauge's other name, conformal Newtonian, comes from [ma1995, mukhanov1992]. The time component of Einstein's equations is Poisson's equation with two terms for the expansion, $
abla^2\Psi - 3\mathcal{H}(\Psi' + \mathcal{H}\Phi) = 4\pi Ga^2\deltaho/c^2$, with $\mathcal{H} = a'/a$ and $\deltaho$ the perturbation of the density [mukhanov1992]. Off the diagonal the space components read $\partial_i\partial_j(\Phi - \Psi) = 0$ for matter with no anisotropic stress, and then the two potentials are one [mukhanov1992, ma1995].¶Evgenii Lifshitz worked out the linear perturbations of the expanding universe in 1946, in coordinates that leave $g_{00}$ and $g_{0i}$ unperturbed, the synchronous gauge [lifshitz1946, ma1995]. Its coordinates are carried by freely falling observers, and where the paths of two of them cross, one event takes two labels [ma1995]. The conditions also leave the first slice of constant time free, and that freedom comes back as solutions of the perturbation equations that describe a change of coordinates and nothing physical [ma1995, mukhanov1992]. The subject, Viatcheslav F. Mukhanov, Hume A. Feldman and Robert H. Brandenberger wrote in 1992, "continued to be plagued by difficulties in interpretation", and the early papers "did not adequately address the gauge freedom" [mukhanov1992].¶Rainer K. Sachs and Arthur M. Wolfe integrated the perturbation equations of a flat Friedmann universe of dust or of radiation and followed light rays through it, in a paper received in May 1966 [sachs1967]. If the microwave radiation is cosmological, they estimated, density fluctuations of order 10 per cent on lengths of order 1000 Mpc would make its temperature vary across the sky by about 1 per cent, through the gravitational redshift and other effects of general relativity [sachs1967]. One term of their redshift is close to an ordinary gravitational redshift, since a function in their metric is "rather similar to a Newtonian potential", and they put it at 0.5 per cent [sachs1967]. In the longitudinal gauge that effect is a temperature fluctuation of $	frac{1}{3}\Phi$, with $\Phi$ taken where the light last scattered, on scales larger than the horizon at that time [mukhanov1992].¶James M. Bardeen settled the gauge question in 1980 with combinations of the perturbations of the metric and the matter that a change of coordinates leaves unchanged [bardeen1980, mukhanov1992, ma1995]. In the longitudinal gauge his $\Phi_A$ and $\Phi_H$ are the potentials themselves, $\Phi = \Phi_A$ and $\Psi = -\Phi_H$ [mukhanov1992, ma1995]. With Paul J. Steinhardt and Michael S. Turner he followed the quantum fluctuations of the scalar field that drives inflation out past the Hubble radius and back in, much of the work done at the Nuffield Workshop on the Very Early Universe in Cambridge in 1982 [bardeen1983]. A fluctuation $\Delta\phi$ of order $H/2\pi$, frozen as its scale crosses the Hubble radius, returns as a density contrast $\deltaho/ho = 4H\Delta\phi/\dot\phi$ if the universe is dominated by radiation when the scale reenters and $	frac{2}{5}H\Delta\phi/\dot\phi$ if it is dominated by matter, with $H$ the Hubble rate and a dot $d/dt$ [bardeen1983]. Between the two crossings their $\zeta$ stays nearly constant, a conservation law that later estimates of the spectrum used [bardeen1983, mukhanov1992]. In the simplest model of new inflation, built on SU(5) grand unification, the contrast came out of order 10 on the scale of the present horizon, and they found a supersymmetric potential that gives $10^{-4}$ to $10^{-3}$ [bardeen1983].¶Mukhanov, Feldman and Brandenberger worked in the longitudinal gauge, where in their words "Bardeen's gauge-invariant variables are identical to the remaining metric variables" [mukhanov1992]. Outside the Hubble radius their $\zeta = 	frac{2}{3}(H^{-1}\dot\Phi + \Phi)/(1 + w) + \Phi$ is conserved, with $w$ the ratio of pressure to energy density, so a potential constant in each era falls to nine tenths of its value as radiation gives way to matter [mukhanov1992]. Chung-Pei Ma and Edmund Bertschinger set the synchronous and longitudinal gauges side by side in 1995, for a universe of cold dark matter, baryons, photons, and massless and massive neutrinos [ma1995]. Freely streaming neutrinos carry most of the anisotropic stress, and outside the horizon in the radiation era they split the potentials to $\Psi = (1 + 	frac{2}{5}R_
u)\Phi$, with $R_
u$ the neutrinos' share of the density of the radiation [ma1995]. Bardeen had worried that a large shear stress would make the metric perturbations of this gauge large, and Ma and Bertschinger showed that free streaming does not do so for the growing mode [ma1995].¶Ma and Bertschinger followed individual neutrinos through the potentials of this gauge from a redshift of about $10^9$ down to $13.5$, to start simulations of structure formation with massive neutrinos [ma1995]. A spectrum with equal power on every scale has index $n = 1$, the Harrison-Zel'dovich spectrum, and the "almost scale-free" spectrum of Bardeen, Steinhardt and Turner lies close to it [ma1995, bardeen1983]. The Planck Collaboration fitted its final maps with a flat universe whose adiabatic scalar perturbations have a power law spectrum, and found the index $n_s = 0.965 \pm 0.004$ [planck2020].

related.text: The unperturbed universe. At $\Phi = \Psi = 0$ the longitudinal gauge is Friedmann's metric in conformal time, with flat space or, through $k$, curved.

The unperturbed universe with a positive cosmological constant alone. At $\Phi = \Psi = 0$ and $a = -c/(H\eta)$, with $\eta < 0$ and $H$ the constant Hubble rate, the flat longitudinal gauge is de Sitter space in flat slices.

A point mass in an expanding universe, exact [mcvittie1933]. To first order in $r_s$ its metric is a Friedmann universe with $\Phi = \Psi = -r_s/2ar$, the potential of a point mass at the proper distance $ar$.
Spherical lumps of dust in an expanding universe, exact at any density contrast [tolman1934, bondi1947].
Lumps of dust in an expanding universe with no symmetry, exact at any density contrast [szekeres1975].

The weak field of a body, a potential laid over flat space as these are laid over an expanding universe. At $a = 1$ its metric to first order in the mass is the longitudinal gauge with $\Phi = -m/r$ and $\Psi = -\gamma m/r$.

parameters.description: Potential in $g_{\eta\eta}$ ($|\Phi| \ll 1$), Bardeen's $\Phi_A$; in the Newtonian limit it is the Newtonian potential over $c^2$
Potential in the metric of space ($|\Psi| \ll 1$), Bardeen's $-\Phi_H$; it equals $\Phi$ wherever the matter carries no anisotropic stress

coordinates.convention: We use the conformal time $\eta$, with $a\,d\eta = c\,dt$, and comoving Cartesian coordinates $(x, y, z)$, all lengths. The gauge and its letters are Mukhanov, Feldman and Brandenberger's longitudinal gauge, written in the signature $(-,+,+,+)$, which is Ma and Bertschinger's conformal Newtonian gauge with their $\psi$ written $\Phi$ and their $\phi$ written $\Psi$. Bardeen's potentials are $\Phi_A = \Phi$ and $\Phi_H = -\Psi$, the signs both papers give.
